summary: Routing healthcheck surge triggering 5xx and runtime restarts for dedicated customer (AtlasMail)
description: Issue summary: AtlasMail observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (primarily 502/503) starting ~2026-03-10 08:40 UTC for requests routed to their dedicated fleet. Impact: user-facing spikes in failed completions and higher latency; customer reports timeouts in production flows. Initial observation correlates with a keystore rotation event and a rapid stream of backend healthcheck probes that coincided with an autoscaler reaction resulting in several serving-runtime restarts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer triggers keystore rollover on their side (cert rotate) during active traffic window
2) Ingress begins to receive increased failed TLS handshakes; api-gateway retries health probes to routed backends
3) Autoscaler interprets flapping as capacity pressure and rapidly scales down then up; several serving-runtime pods enter restart loops
4) Requests to the affected tenant see 502/503 from proxy and upstream runtime restarts, amplifying error rate
observed_behavior: Between 08:40–09:10 UTC error rate for tenantAtlasMail rose to 8% 5xx with cluster-level runtime restart spikes. Grafana panels show accept queue drop and a short burst of connection resets from api-gateway. Traces show time spent waiting on upstream connection and 'upstream reset' messages.
expected_behavior: Normal error rate <0.1% and no runtime restarts during a keystore rotation; healthchecks should not precipitate autoscaler oscillation.
logs: [prod-us-west][08:41:12] proxy: upstream reset while sending request to runtime-xyz-3 (502)
[08:42:01] serving-runtime: watchdog: restarting due to lost GPU lease (observed right after SIGTERM during scale-down)
[08:43:05] autoscaler: rapid scale-down detected (expected cooldown missing) -> scale-up triggered at 08:43:21
investigation_notes: Support triage: verified customer timeline and captured request ids; customer confirmed keystore rotation at 08:39 UTC
SRE: api-gateway started a flurry of health probe retries to the dedicated fleet after seeing TLS handshake failures (likely from the cert rotation transient)

SRE hypothesis: healthcheck retry burst increased ephemeral connection churn which exposed flaky keepalive handling in the proxy -> backpressure to the runtime -> autoscaler misinterpreted metrics and triggered churn
Observed that cooldown window for the autoscaler policy for this dedicated pool was set to a short 15s (below recommended 120s) — amplifies oscillation risk
Runtime logs show multiple restarts tied to eviction during aggressive scale-down; restart sequence made the fleet temporarily unhealthy leading to 502 amplification
comments: [2026-03-10 09:02 UTC] Maya Chen (Support): Customer reports 5xx spike after rotating certs. Collected sample request ids and asked for timeline. Escalating to SRE.

[2026-03-10 09:18 UTC] Nora Patel (SRE): Confirmed healthcheck retry storm from api-gateway at 08:40. Notable: backend servers returned TLS handshake failures for ~40s. Attached gateway dump and grafana link.

[2026-03-10 09:45 UTC] Liam O'Connor (Oncall Infra): Found autoscaler cooldown set to 15s for this dedicated pool. Increasing to 180s as a temporary mitigation to stop oscillation. Noted related runtime restarts correlated with aggressive scale-down events.

[2026-03-10 10:10 UTC] AtlasMail (customer): Confirmed keystore rotation did not complete cleanly for one instance; restarting their side fixed TLS failures. Appreciative of SRE mitigations; experiencing reduced errors.

[2026-03-11 14:22 UTC] Engineering (serving-runtime): Reproduced accept-queue exhaustion in staging by simulating rapid healthprobe retries and short autoscaler cooldown. Created a PR to add backoff to healthcheck retries and to harden keepalive handling (see linked PR).
[2026-03-12 08:30 UTC] Liam O'Connor: Temporarily applied autoscaler cooldown policy change across dedicated pools where cooldown <60s. Monitoring for regression.
resolution_notes: Mitigations applied: 1) increased autoscaler cooldown for the affected dedicated pool to 180s to stop rapid churn; 2) customer rolled back and retried keystore rotation and confirmed TLS success; 3) temporary rate-limiting added to api-gateway healthcheck retries for tenant-scoped routing. Root cause appears to be a combination of customer-side transient TLS failures + overly aggressive autoscaler cooldown + insufficient backoff on healthcheck retries. Engineering PR submitted to add backoff and improve proxy keepalive handling.
next_steps: Monitor error rate and runtime restart counts for AtlasMail for 72 hours
Ship PR 842 to staging and run chaos tests to validate healthcheck backoff under similar conditions
Audit other dedicated pools for autoscaler cooldowns <60s and raise to recommended defaults
Coordinate with Customer Success to add keystore rotation checklist to Dedicated onboarding docs
